scope: Public-purpose summaries plus editorial synthetic training scenarios. Not a technical manual, configuration authority, readiness certification or automatic impact prediction. Confirm equipment variants and approved procedures. Do not enter operational data.

records.name: STT
records.purpose: Provides satellite transport for a supported network node.
records.mission: Connect a command post to remote headquarters when the approved network design uses SATCOM.
records.path: Power and site → terminal acquisition → authorized access → node handoff → remote service
records.why: Antenna acquisition does not prove two-way network access.
records.impact: The satellite path is unavailable; local command post services may still work.
records.consequence: Remote reporting and data exchange using this path are disrupted.
records.remaining: Local services and independently tested alternate transport.
records.proof: Verify terminal status and the node handoff, then exchange a report with a remote endpoint.
records.scenario: Receive lock is indicated, but a remote application cannot be reached.
records.lesson: Do not report all communications lost. Identify which path and services have actually failed.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved STT training baseline. Verify terminal status and the node handoff, then exchange a report with a remote endpoint. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using STT. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: Receive lock is indicated, but a remote application cannot be reached. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why STT is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: The STT indicates receive lock, but our remote application test failed. That does not yet identify whether the fault is in satellite access, the network path or the application. The tested remote exchange is unavailable to the affected staff users. Local services and alternates need separate checks. We are tracing the failed path and will request the responsible owner’s help when isolated. Restoration time is unknown; next update in 15 minutes.

records.name: JNN
records.purpose: Connects command post users and systems to a wider tactical network; traditionally a brigade node.
records.mission: Provide the approved network access needed for staff coordination and reporting.
records.path: Power → LAN/VLANs → routing/security path → transport → remote services
records.why: A healthy physical interface does not prove correct VLANs, routes or a return path.
records.impact: The affected network path can isolate multiple staff systems.
records.consequence: Reports, coordination and application exchanges using that path may be delayed.
records.remaining: Unaffected local networks and validated alternate communications.
records.proof: Test an endpoint, gateway, remote address and required application separately.
records.scenario: Local users reach their gateway but cannot reach remote services.
records.lesson: Separate a shared upstream fault from individual application failures.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved JNN training baseline. Test an endpoint, gateway, remote address and required application separately. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using JNN. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: Local users reach their gateway but cannot reach remote services. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why JNN is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: Tested local users can reach their gateway but cannot reach the remote service. We have not established that every remote destination is affected. The staff cannot complete the tested digital exchange. Local gateway reachability is confirmed; an alternate reporting path has not been validated. We are checking the WAN handoff, routes and return path with the responsible owners. Restoration time is unknown; next update in 15 minutes.

records.name: CPN
records.purpose: Provides battalion command post access to the tactical network in the applicable architecture.
records.mission: Connect battalion staff services with higher headquarters and remote users.
records.path: Power → local access → approved routing/security baseline → transport → service test
records.why: A working local LAN does not establish battalion-to-brigade connectivity.
records.impact: The battalion can lose remote network access while retaining local services.
records.consequence: Routine digital reporting and receipt of remote updates can stop.
records.remaining: Local services and separately verified voice or alternate data paths.
records.proof: Exchange a synthetic report with higher headquarters and confirm receipt.
records.scenario: Local collaboration works, but the remote report is not delivered.
records.lesson: State which exchange failed and whether priority reporting has a verified alternative.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved CPN training baseline. Exchange a synthetic report with higher headquarters and confirm receipt. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using CPN. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: Local collaboration works, but the remote report is not delivered. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why CPN is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: Local collaboration works, but the battalion’s test report was not delivered to the remote recipient. The staff cannot rely on that reporting exchange yet. We have not isolated the failed component or verified an alternate. We are checking the path and confirming whether the recipient’s service is available. We need the recipient to participate in the retest. Restoration time is unknown; next update in 15 minutes.

records.name: BCCS
records.purpose: Legacy server infrastructure supporting mission command services.
records.mission: Host the services required by the supported staff; confirm the actual legacy baseline.
records.path: Power/cooling → hardware/storage → host environment → common services → applications
records.why: Server power does not prove that hosted services or databases are available.
records.impact: A shared server dependency may affect several staff applications.
records.consequence: Staff members may lose access to collaboration, stored information or application services.
records.remaining: Unaffected services and approved manual or alternate reporting methods, after validation.
records.proof: Check required services and have a staff user complete a synthetic task.
records.scenario: The stack is powered, but multiple users cannot open a required service.
records.lesson: Report the failed service and user task rather than calling every network link down.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved BCCS training baseline. Check required services and have a staff user complete a synthetic task. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using BCCS. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: The stack is powered, but multiple users cannot open a required service. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why BCCS is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: The server stack is powered on, but several test users cannot open the required service. The staff task using that service is disrupted; we have not shown that the entire network is down. We are checking shared server dependencies and will coordinate with the application owner. Other services and alternates need separate validation. Restoration time is unknown; next update in 15 minutes.

records.name: TSI
records.purpose: Server infrastructure hosting CPCE and critical common services.
records.mission: Support command post applications and information exchange for staff work.
records.path: Power/cooling → storage/virtualization → network → common services → CPCE/data exchange
records.why: A running virtual machine does not establish healthy application or synchronization services.
records.impact: Application access or remote data synchronization may be degraded.
records.consequence: The staff may act on stale information if update age is not recognized.
records.remaining: Verified local functions and independent reporting channels.
records.proof: Verify service health, remote update timestamps and completion of a staff task.
records.scenario: The COP opens, but remote updates have stopped.
records.lesson: A visible COP is not proof that the information is current.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved TSI training baseline. Verify service health, remote update timestamps and completion of a staff task. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using TSI. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: The COP opens, but remote updates have stopped. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why TSI is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: CPCE opens, but remote updates have stopped. The staff can see the display, but should treat remote information as potentially stale and check its timestamp before using it. We have not isolated the synchronization failure or verified an alternate update method. We are checking the data exchange with the remote owner. Restoration time is unknown; next update in 15 minutes. Recovery will include a fresh remote update confirmed by the staff.

records.name: JBC-P
records.purpose: Mounted situational awareness, mapping and messaging system.
records.mission: Support mounted reporting and exchange of position and situational information.
records.path: Vehicle power/wiring → computer/display → position source → communications → messaging
records.why: A map can display without a healthy remote communications path.
records.impact: Mounted messages or remote situational updates may fail while navigation remains available.
records.consequence: Leaders may have delayed reports or stale awareness of other platforms.
records.remaining: Verified own-position functions and independent communications.
records.proof: Confirm valid position, send a message, obtain receipt and inspect update age.
records.scenario: Own position displays, but remote tracks are stale and a message is undelivered.
records.lesson: Distinguish position availability from remote information exchange.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved JBC-P training baseline. Confirm valid position, send a message, obtain receipt and inspect update age. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using JBC-P. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: Own position displays, but remote tracks are stale and a message is undelivered. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why JBC-P is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: The display shows our own position, but remote tracks are stale and the test message is undelivered. We have not independently verified position accuracy. Mounted leaders cannot rely on current remote updates or that message path. An alternate communications method still needs testing. We are separating the position-source, transport and messaging checks. Restoration time is unknown; next update in 15 minutes.

records.name: MMC-S
records.purpose: Mounted Mission Command software modernizing the mounted application environment.
records.mission: Support mounted mission command tasks on the fielded computing and transport baseline.
records.path: Approved software baseline → platform identity/position → available transport → data exchange
records.why: A software upgrade does not establish that new transport hardware was installed.
records.impact: The application may be usable locally while remote exchange fails.
records.consequence: Mounted coordination may rely on incomplete or delayed information.
records.remaining: Tested local functions and separately verified transport alternatives.
records.proof: Validate a synthetic message and remote update through the installed transport.
records.scenario: The application starts, but remote messages do not arrive.
records.lesson: Identify the installed software, compute and transport boundaries before assigning the fault.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved MMC-S training baseline. Validate a synthetic message and remote update through the installed transport. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using MMC-S. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: The application starts, but remote messages do not arrive. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why MMC-S is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: MMC-S starts, but remote test messages are not arriving. Local application startup is confirmed; remote exchange is not. Mounted staff may miss reports through that path. We are identifying the installed compute and transport baseline before assigning the fault. We have not validated an alternate or a restoration estimate. We will coordinate a two-way test with the recipient and provide the next update in 15 minutes.

records.name: TRILOS
records.mission: Provide an approved terrestrial path between nodes, including transport diversity where designed.
records.path: Site/path → mast/antenna → compatible radio configuration → RF link → Ethernet/IP handoff
records.why: RF link establishment does not prove that the connected IP network is configured correctly.
records.impact: The terrestrial path may be unavailable or unstable.
records.consequence: Traffic using this path can be delayed or redirected onto a lower-capacity alternative.
records.remaining: Other validated paths; capacity must be checked before claiming equivalent service.
records.proof: Inspect RF/link evidence and then validate the remote service across the handoff.
records.scenario: Radio link status is healthy, but users cannot pass data.
records.lesson: Investigate the data handoff instead of assuming antenna alignment is the cause.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved TRILOS training baseline. Inspect RF/link evidence and then validate the remote service across the handoff. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using TRILOS. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: Radio link status is healthy, but users cannot pass data. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why TRILOS is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: TRILOS reports a radio link, but our end-to-end data test fails. That indication does not prove the Ethernet and IP handoff works. Users cannot complete the tested exchange through this path. We have not established that antenna alignment is the cause or that another path has sufficient capacity. We are checking the handoff with the network owner. Restoration time is unknown; next update in 15 minutes.

records.name: SINCGARS
records.purpose: VHF combat net voice and data radio family.
records.mission: Support the assigned net and required command-and-control exchanges.
records.path: Power/audio/antenna → approved mode/net configuration → synchronization/security readiness → radio check
records.why: Frequency hopping, time alignment and encryption have distinct functions.
records.impact: A station or net segment may be unable to exchange required traffic.
records.consequence: Reports and coordination may be delayed even when a radio powers on normally.
records.remaining: Other stations and alternate communications only after checks.
records.proof: Use the applicable operator procedure and complete an intelligible two-way radio check.
records.scenario: One station cannot communicate while other stations on the net can.
records.lesson: Establish whether the fault is local before declaring the entire net unavailable.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved SINCGARS training baseline. Use the applicable operator procedure and complete an intelligible two-way radio check. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using SINCGARS. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: One station cannot communicate while other stations on the net can. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why SINCGARS is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: One station failed its radio check while other net members can communicate. We have not shown that the entire net is unavailable. Reports from that station may be delayed. We are checking that station using the applicable operator procedure and coordinating another two-way check. Its alternate method is not yet verified. Restoration time is unknown; next update in 15 minutes.

records.name: HF
records.purpose: A radio communications category using propagation and antennas suited to the intended path.
records.mission: Provide an authorized voice or data path, including beyond-line-of-sight communications when conditions support it.
records.path: Requirement/path → authorized frequencies/mode → antenna/feedline/coupler → radio configuration → contact
records.why: Successful antenna tuning does not prove a usable propagation path; ALE cannot create one.
records.impact: The intended HF path may not support contact or the required data service.
records.consequence: A contingency reporting method may be unavailable or slower than planned.
records.remaining: Other verified paths and any lower-rate service actually demonstrated.
records.proof: Validate contact and the required voice/data exchange; record conditions and limitations.
records.scenario: The antenna tunes successfully, but the destination cannot be contacted.
records.lesson: Check the complete path and propagation assumptions rather than equating tuning with connectivity.

exercises.COMMEX: Bring up the approved HF training baseline. Validate contact and the required voice/data exchange; record conditions and limitations. Identify what each indicator proves and what remains untested.
exercises.STAFFEX: Have the supported staff complete a reporting or coordination task using HF. Confirm the recipient can use the information, not just that it was sent.
exercises.WFX: Inject this synthetic fault: The antenna tunes successfully, but the destination cannot be contacted. Brief the affected staff task, validated alternatives and next update. Restore service and have the staff validate recovery.
exercises.Mission rehearsal: Explain why HF is required for the fictional mission, who depends on it, and how its loss changes the communications plan. Rehearse the alternate before declaring it available.

records.brief_example: The antenna tunes, but we have not established contact with the destination. A successful tune does not prove a usable propagation path. The intended HF reporting exchange is unavailable in this test. We are checking the approved mode, antenna arrangement and propagation assumptions with the distant station. No alternate or restoration estimate is verified yet. Next update in 15 minutes; recovery requires the intended voice or data exchange.
